# GPU Radar — DSH plugin
A DSH plugin that answers one question: **who is using this machine's GPU, and which model or job ow
answers one question: **who is using this machine's GPU, and which model or job owns that memory.**
A small badge sits to the left of the input box with live GPU / VRAM / CPU readings. Click it and a
panel opens: VRAM is grouped by **project**, and each project drills down into its processes, the mo
dels it has loaded and the jobs it is running. From there you can pause, resume or kill processes, a
nd pin a VRAM budget per project.
*Shot from the standalone web build of the same panel; as a plugin it renders as a popover next to t
standalone web build of the same panel; as a plugin it renders as a popover next to the input box.*
## Features
- Three dials — GPU utilisation, VRAM in use, CPU utilisation — each with a 0–100% mini trend line u

nderneath
- RAM bar plus one load column per core
- Project leaderboard sorted by VRAM; two bars per

row (VRAM and CPU), sortable by CPU or RAM
- Project detail: member processes with VRAM / CPU / RAM

/ peak, a runtime overview, loaded models, running jobs
- Process control: pause, resume, kill — fo

r one process or the whole project
- VRAM budgets: cap a project, over-budget rows go red; reserved

headroom with a one-click suggested value
- Follows the host theme, light and dark
- Bilingual panel
: English unless the active DSH locale is Chinese

Copy this repository to `~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-gpu-governor/` first. Editing `lib/client.js` only needs
a page refresh; changing `lib/index.js` or `lib/*.ps1` needs a client restart.
## Use
The badge shows the busiest reading at a glance. The refresh button pulls a sample manually; the pan
el otherwise samples every 4 seconds. Kill requires a second click on the same button. `Esc` walks b
ack out of the detail view.
| Question | Where the answer is |

| How much GPU / CPU / RAM is in use? | The three dials and the RAM bar |
| Who is holding VRAM? | L

eaderboard rows are **projects**, not PIDs |
| Is it also burning CPU? | Two bars per row: VRAM and

CPU |
| Which processes belong to this project? | Click a row: PID, VRAM, CPU, RAM, pause / kill |
|
**Which model or job is it actually running?** | Detail view: runtime overview, loaded models, runn

ing jobs |
| How much can I still allocate? | Dial footnote: allocatable = free VRAM − reserved head

room |
| How did it get here? | The scope trace: last 10 minutes of VRAM (solid) and CPU (dashed) |
## Where the numbers come from
Under WDDM, per-process VRAM from `nvidia-smi` is always `[N/A]`, so per-process figures come from t
he driver performance counters instead.
| Metric | Source |

| Per-process VRAM | `Win32_PerfFormattedData_GPUPerformanceCounters_GPUProcessMemory` |
| Per-proce

ss GPU utilisation | The matching `...GPUEngine` class |
| Card-level VRAM, temperature, power | `nv

idia-smi --query-gpu` |
| Per-process CPU and RAM | `Win32_Process`, delta of KernelModeTime and Use

rModeTime |
| Process product name | The exe's PE resource `FileDescription`, cached by path |
| Mac

hine and per-core CPU | `Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_Processor` |
| RAM | `Win32_OperatingSystem`

ne and per-core CPU | `Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_Processor` |
| RAM | `Win32_OperatingSystem` |
The collector is a resident PowerShell child process (`lib/collector.ps1`) that prints one JSON line
per round. Fields the host does not recognise are ignored, so the two halves can be updated indepen
dently. One round takes a few hundred milliseconds to about a second, every 4 seconds by default.
## Project grouping
Command lines carry evidence of different strength, so they are bucketed first and the rules run in
carry evidence of different strength, so they are bucketed first and the rules run in bucket order:
| Bucket | Example | Meaning |
| `script` | `D:\AI\ComfyUI\main.py`, `ArenaDemo.uproject` | What is running — the strongest evidenc

e |
| `binary` | `...\Programs\Python311\python.exe` | The interpreter or program, i.e. only which s

oftware is in use |
| `arg` | `--user-data-dir=...\Roaming\@deepseek-ai` | A directory in the argume
nts — the weakest evidence |
Rule order: `workspace` → `desktop` → `path` (AI, Projects, UEProjects, models, …) → `software` → dr
ive root → `exe` → `system`. So `python.exe D:\AI\ComfyUI-H3\main.py` becomes ComfyUI-H3, and `Unrea
lEditor-Cmd.exe ...\ArenaDemo.uproject` becomes ArenaDemo.

## Runtime overview
Numbers alone do not say what something is, so after each sample the host makes bounded local probes
and attaches the result to the project. A closed port or a timeout only costs detail, never the res
the result to the project. A closed port or a timeout only costs detail, never the resource numbers.
| Source | Endpoint | Gives |
| FlowEdge | `127.0.0.1:8080/api/health`, `/api/deps`, `/api/runs?status=running`, `/api/pipelines`

| Engine version and uptime, dependency services, running runs |
| ComfyUI | Dependency endpoint plu

s `/queue`, `/system_stats`, `/history` | Queue, device VRAM, weights used by the last execution |
|
Weight files | `<install>/models/**` and directories from `extra_model_paths.yaml` | On-disk size p

er weight file |
| Ollama | `127.0.0.1:11434/api/ps` | Resident model names, VRAM and size |
ComfyUI attribution stacks three layers of evidence: `ckpt_name`, `unet_name`, `vae_name` and `lora_
name` from prompts in `/queue`; otherwise the latest entry of `/history`, ordered by the timestamps
in `status.messages`, because ComfyUI does not unload weights on its own; sizes are stat'ed per mode
l root and cached. When the weight total exceeds resident VRAM the panel says the remainder is swapp
ed in on demand instead of inventing an active/resident split.
Bases can be overridden with `flowedgeBaseUrl`, `ollamaBaseUrl`, or the `FLOWEDGE_BASE_URL` and `OLL
AMA_BASE_URL` environment variables. `probeServices: false` turns probing off entirely.
